entries.with of: of is obligatory — ✗ a plurality voters. The noun after of is normally definite or generic: a plurality of the votes, a plurality of Americans. Bare a plurality is common with the set understood: She won a plurality.
entries.pattern: a plurality of [plural countable] · a plurality of [the + plural] · win / take a plurality of the vote · patent claim: comprising a plurality of [noun]
entries.contrast: Two technical senses, and neither means what it looks like. 1. In elections a plurality is the largest share, not necessarily a majority: a candidate who takes 42 percent of a three-way race has a plurality and not a majority, and that distinction is what decides whether a runoff is required. 2. In United States patent practice a plurality of means simply two or more — a plurality of vents claims at least two vents and nothing more — which is why patent claims are full of a phrase that in ordinary English sounds like a crowd. Do not reach for it as a formal synonym for many: a reader in either field will read it as a number.
entries.variants: a majority of, pluralities of, win by a plurality, a plurality (bare)
entries.see also: a majority of, a supermajority of, a quorum of, most, the majority of, the minority of

entries.meaning: The number of a body's members that must be present before it can transact business — a threshold fixed by rule, not by the speaker.
examples: A quorum of the board was present, and the meeting was called to order.
Without a quorum of the members, the committee may debate but cannot vote.
The bylaws set a quorum of five, which the club has not managed since March.
A quorum of the commission failed to appear and the hearing was continued.
The clerk noted the absence of a quorum and the chamber adjourned.
State law requires a quorum of two-thirds for any vote to amend the charter.
entries.pronunciation note: of reduces to /ə/: /ə ˈkwɔrəmə/
entries.русский: кворум — число членов, необходимое для правомочности заседания
entries.register: technical — parliamentary procedure, corporate governance, statutes, and the minutes of any body that meets and votes. Neutral inside that world and out of place outside it
entries.goes with: plural countable nouns naming the members of a defined body — a quorum of the board, a quorum of members, a quorum of the senate. It cannot take an uncountable noun (✗ a quorum of money) and cannot take a set with no membership rule behind it (✗ a quorum of customers).
entries.with of: of is obligatory when the body is named — ✗ a quorum the board. Bare a quorum with the body understood is the commoner form in practice: We have a quorum, A quorum was present, The meeting lacked a quorum.
entries.pattern: a quorum of [the + defined body] · a quorum was present · lack / constitute / establish a quorum · in the absence of a quorum
entries.contrast: A quorum is a minimum, and the minimum is set elsewhere — by statute, charter, or bylaws — so the phrase names a number without telling you what it is: a quorum may be a majority, two-thirds, or five people in a room. That is what separates it from a majority of, which is arithmetic and needs no governing document. Note what the threshold is for: a quorum makes a body able to act at all, which is a separate question from how many votes any particular motion then needs. The verb is singular, since quorum is the head noun: A quorum of the board was present. The word is Latin for "of whom," lifted out of the wording of old commissions.
entries.variants: a quorum, quorum call, lack a quorum, quorate (chiefly British)
entries.see also: a supermajority of, a plurality of, a majority of, enough, all

entries.meaning: A share of a body larger than a simple majority, at a level fixed by statute, charter, or bylaws.
examples: Overriding the veto takes a supermajority of both chambers.
The bylaws require a supermajority of shareholders to approve any sale of assets.
A supermajority of the council voted to rezone the block over the mayor's objection.
The measure fell two votes short of a supermajority.
Several states require a supermajority of the legislature to raise any tax.
A supermajority of three-fifths is written into the district's charter.
entries.pronunciation note: main stress on -jor-, secondary stress on su-; the t flaps to /ɾ/ as in majority
entries.русский: квалифицированное большинство — доля больше простого большинства
entries.register: technical — constitutional and corporate law, legislative reporting, and bylaws. It has become common enough in political journalism since the 1970s that most Americans meet it every budget season
entries.goes with: plural countable nouns naming members or votes — a supermajority of the senate, a supermajority of shareholders, a supermajority of the votes cast. Never an uncountable noun: ✗ a supermajority of support.
entries.with of: of is obligatory when the body is named — ✗ a supermajority the senate. Bare a supermajority is common with the body understood: The amendment needs a supermajority.
entries.pattern: a supermajority of [the + body] · a two-thirds / three-fifths supermajority of [body] · require / reach / fall short of a supermajority · supermajority requirement
entries.contrast: A supermajority is any threshold above a simple majority, and like a quorum the actual fraction is set by the governing document — most often two-thirds, sometimes three-fifths or three-quarters. That puts the three threshold words in a series: a plurality is the largest share, a majority is more than half, a supermajority is more than a majority by a stated amount. The verb is singular, since supermajority is the head noun: A supermajority of the members was required. The word is American and modern; older documents simply say a two-thirds vote.
entries.variants: a two-thirds supermajority, a three-fifths supermajority, supermajority requirement, a majority of
entries.see also: a majority of, a plurality of, a quorum of, most, the majority of, the minority of

entries.meaning: The part of something, and only that part, which meets the stated condition — the legal drafter's way of quantifying by definition instead of by number.
examples: So much of the appropriation as remains unexpended on June 30 shall revert to the general fund.
So much of the Act as relates to licensing takes effect immediately.
The trustee shall distribute so much of the income as is necessary for the beneficiary's support.
So many of the directors as are present may adjourn the meeting to a later date.
The court considered so much of the record as had been designated on appeal.
A plain-language redraft says the same thing: the part of the appropriation that is unspent reverts.
entries.pronunciation note: read aloud, the as is normally weak, /əz/, and of reduces to /əv/ or /ə/
entries.русский: юр.: в той части, в какой… — только та часть, которая отвечает условию
entries.position: central — so much fills the determiner slot and the as-clause that completes it follows the noun
entries.register: legal and formal — the ordinary drafting idiom of statutes, wills, appropriations, and contracts, and stiff to the point of parody anywhere else. Plain-language drafting is steadily replacing it with the part of … that
entries.goes with: uncountable nouns and mass-like abstractions in the much version — so much of the fund as remains, so much of the Act as relates to fees. The countable version is so many … as: so many of the directors as are present. Never a bare singular countable noun.
entries.with of: of is obligatory, and so is the as-clause: both halves are required. ✗ so much of the fund alone is incomplete, and so much as by itself is a different construction entirely, an emphatic negative-polarity item meaning "even" (he never so much as looked at it).
entries.pattern: so much of [the + noun] as [verb phrase] · so many of [the + plural] as [verb phrase] · plain-language equivalent: the part of [noun] that [verb phrase]
entries.contrast: The frame is a restrictive quantifier: it does not report a quantity, it carves one out. So much of the appropriation as is unexpended means exactly the unexpended part and no more, which is why drafters reach for it — they must define a share without knowing its size. Keep it clear of two lookalikes. So much as on its own means "even" and needs a negative to lean on. As much … as is the ordinary comparative: as much of the fund as we can spare compares two amounts, where so much of the fund as remains defines one. In your own prose, write the part of the fund that remains.
entries.variants: so many … as, so much as (= even), as much … as, such … as
entries.see also: much, most, enough, a quorum of, so, too, as
